{{Short description|American theoretical physicist}}
'''Thomas Witten''' is an American theoretical [[physicist]] working in the field of [[soft matter]] physics.

==Biography==
Witten received his doctorate in physics in 1971 from the [[University of California, San Diego]].
He is currently the Homer J. Livingston Professor in the [[James Franck Institute]] at the [[University of Chicago]].
He is known in particular for his work on [[diffusion-limited aggregation]],<ref>{{cite journal
|url=http://prl.aps.org/abstract/PRL/v47/i19/p1400_1
|title=Diffusion-Limited Aggregation, a Kinetic Critical Phenomenon
|author1=T. A. Witten, Jr.  |author2=L. M. Sander
 |name-list-style=amp |year=1981
|journal=Physical Review Letters
|volume=47
|issue=19
|pages=1400–1403|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.47.1400
|bibcode=1981PhRvL..47.1400W
|url-access=subscription
}}
</ref> crumpled sheets<ref>{{cite journal
|url=http://rmp.aps.org/abstract/RMP/v79/i2/p643_1
|title=Stress focusing in elastic sheets
|author=Thomas A. Witten
|year=2007
|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics
|volume=79
|issue=2
|pages=643–675
|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.79.643
|bibcode=2007RvMP...79..643W
|url-access=subscription
}}</ref> and coffee rings.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.uchicago.edu/|title=University of Chicago News|website=news.uchicago.edu}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
|url=https://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v389/n6653/abs/389827a0.html
|title=Capillary flow as the cause of ring stains from dried liquid drops
|author1 = Robert D. Deegan
|author2 = [[Olgica Bakajin]]
|author3 =  Todd F. Dupont
|author4 =  Greg Huber
|author5 = Sidney R. Nagel
|author6 = Thomas A. Witten
|year=1997
|journal=Nature
|volume=389
|issue=6653
|pages=827–829
|doi=10.1038/39827
|bibcode=1997Natur.389..827D
|s2cid=205027233
|url-access=subscription
}}</ref>
His current research interests include polymers, complex fluids and granular materials.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.uchicago.edu/profile/thomas-witten|title=University of Chicago News Profile}}</ref>
He cowrote the "Structured Fluids: Polymers, Colloids, Surfactants" ({{ISBN|019958382X}}) together with [[Philip Pincus]].

In 2002 he received the [[American Physical Society]] Polymer Physics Prize<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm|title=Prize Recipient|website=www.aps.org}}</ref> and he is an elected fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].
In 2010 he held the Lorentz Chair at [[Leiden University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lorentz.leidenuniv.nl/lorentzchair/|title=Lorentz Chair since 1955|website=www.lorentz.leidenuniv.nl}}</ref>
